title: Hard Examples Beat Easy Examples in Repetition-Heavy Long-CoT Fine-Tuning

contributions.purpose: Determine which examples should be selected when training long-CoT models with many-epoch repetition on small datasets.
contributions.mechanism: NLL-based data selection comparison on OLMo3-7B with Dolci-Think, training length-matched 800-example subsets (low-NLL, high-NLL, random) for 32 epochs under identical conditions.
contributions.evaluation: High-NLL (hard-to-fit) examples significantly outperform low-NLL examples, 33.0% vs. 23.6% aggregate accuracy on AIME and GPQA benchmarks, consistent across mathematical and scientific reasoning.
contributions.domain: LLM long chain-of-thought fine-tuning / data selection
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that high-NLL examples significantly outperform low-NLL examples (33.0% vs. 23.6% aggregate accuracy) under repetition-heavy training, contradicting the intuition that easy-to-fit examples are preferable.

contributions.purpose: Explain why low-NLL selection fails under repetition-heavy training.
contributions.mechanism: Confound analysis linking low-NLL examples to high textual repetition and its effects on training dynamics.
contributions.evaluation: Low-NLL examples exhibit trigram repetition rate 0.457 vs. 0.206, leading to poor termination behavior and unstable training dynamics; hyperparameter tuning and trigram filtering fail to recover low-NLL performance.
contributions.domain: LLM long chain-of-thought fine-tuning / data selection
contributions.source_quote: We identify a critical confound: low-NLL examples exhibit high textual repetition (trigram rate 0.457 vs. 0.206), leading to poor termination behavior and unstable training dynamics.

contributions.purpose: Give practitioners actionable guidance for repetition-heavy fine-tuning regimes.
contributions.mechanism: Distilling the empirical comparison into a selection rule for many-epoch training on small datasets.
contributions.evaluation: Supported by the 33.0% vs. 23.6% aggregate accuracy gap and the failure of optimization attempts (hyperparameter tuning, trigram filtering) to rescue low-NLL selection.
contributions.domain: LLM long chain-of-thought fine-tuning / data selection
contributions.source_quote: We provide practical guidance for repetition-heavy training: select hard-to-fit examples rather than easy-to-fit ones when using many-epoch repetition on small datasets.

self_declared_provenance.quote: A surprising finding from Kopiczko et al. (2026) shows that repetition-heavy training—fine-tuning on a small subset of examples for many epochs—can match or exceed the performance of training on larger datasets... This raises a fundamental question: when training with many-epoch repetition, which examples should be selected for the training subset?
However, existing methods focus primarily on single-epoch training regimes and do not address the interaction between data selection and many-epoch repetition, which is the focus of our work.

notes: Pure empirical/analysis paper (all contributions are findings; no new method proposed). Contains a negative result for the low-NLL selection strategy: hyperparameter tuning and trigram filtering fail to recover its performance, indicating a fundamental limitation.
